findings.suggested: In 1946, Peggy Carter, grieving Steve Rogers, is stuck fetching lunch orders at the Strategic Scientific Reserve in New York. When Howard Stark is accused of selling his weapons to America's enemies, she secretly works with his butler, Edwin Jarvis, to clear his name. The trail leads to Leviathan, a Soviet group that trained girls like Dottie Underwood as assassins, and to Johann Fennhoff, who hypnotizes Howard into flying poison gas over Times Square. Peggy talks him down and finally lets Steve go, pouring the last vial of his blood into the East River.

findings.suggested: Reed Richards, Johnny Storm, Ben Grimm and Victor Von Doom teleport to Planet Zero, and the trip home gives Reed, Johnny, Ben and Sue Storm powers. Victor, left behind, comes back to destroy Earth. On the TVA's monitors, Earth-15866 is marked terminated.

findings.current: ... and the royal family is scattered across Hawaii before taking it back.
findings.problem: They do not take Attilan back: Black Bolt locks Maximus in the bunker and the Inhumans evacuate to Earth as Attilan is destroyed.
findings.suggested: Black Bolt, king of the Inhumans' moon city, Attilan, is overthrown by his brother Maximus. The royal family, scattered across Hawaii, regroups, locks Maximus away and leads its people to Earth as Attilan falls.

findings.current: Eddie and Venom are on the run from the military and from Knull, the creator of the symbiotes.
findings.problem: Knull never chases them; he is imprisoned and sends Xenophages to Earth to take the Codex they carry.
findings.suggested: Eddie and Venom are on the run from the military and from the Xenophages that Knull, the creator of the symbiotes, sends to find them. Venom sacrifices himself to save Eddie.

findings.current: Silvermane's men become the Sandman and Megawatt.
findings.problem: Flint Marko already turns to sand in episode 1, as Cat Hardy's bodyguard, and Dirk Leyden is a criminal with electric powers before Marko frees him to join Silvermane (episode 5); neither gains powers as Silvermane's man. The names Sandman and Megawatt are not used in any episode summary checked. The Faber clause is defensible (every metahuman saw her before their powers appeared, and her failed cure aggravated their conditions).
findings.suggested: Replace that sentence with: 'Flint Marko, who can turn to sand, and Dirk Leyden, who feeds on electricity, end up fighting for Silvermane.'
findings.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Noir (episode summaries E1, E4, E5, E8)

Valentina announces the team, not Yelena as its leader. Wikipedia calls Bucky the team's de facto leader.
findings.suggested: Years later, Yelena is still working for Valentina. Sent to a vault on what she thinks is one last kill, she finds other expendable assets sent to kill her, and a strange man named Bob. ... Valentina announces them to the press as the New Avengers.

findings.suggested: If no scene makes her leader: "Natasha: deceased. Yelena: one of the *New Avengers" [from Thunderbolts*] and "Natasha: deceased. Yelena: a *New Avenger, digging into Damage Control" [from Spider-Man: Brand New Day]

findings.current: Spider-Man visits her for help with a strange clue ... By the end, she's helping gather evidence against the Department of Damage Control.

Later, mid-film, she finds in redacted Damage Control files that Jean Grey's sister Sara was a telepath who died in its experiments.
findings.suggested: Yelena works out of a New York bathhouse now. When Spider-Man comes to her about an attack on a Damage Control prison, she says it's too small for her team, but tells him someone keeps hitting Damage Control sites looking for "V-Max". Later she digs through Damage Control's redacted files and learns that Jean Grey's sister, Sara, died in its experiments.

findings.current: ...but he's slipping back toward the savage, uncontrollable Hulk. ... Jean Grey ... takes control of the Hulk to break into director Bill Metzger's vault, and the Hulk overpowers Spider-Man. Peter reaches the Hulk ... and Bruce takes back control.
findings.problem: Nothing shows Bruce slipping before Jean. She possesses him as Smart Hulk to attack Damage Control's headquarters, then possesses Frank Castle to open a vault hiding Damage Control agents. Freed, Bruce turns back to human, but his inhibitor is smashed and he becomes the savage Hulk. Peter calms him, and Bruce is taken to a hospital for psychiatric care.
findings.suggested: Fully human again, Bruce teaches at Empire State University and wears an inhibitor to keep the Hulk down. Peter Parker, a stranger to Bruce, comes to him for help with his own changing powers. Jean Grey, a telepath at war with Damage Control, takes over Bruce's mind to attack its headquarters, and when she lets go, his broken inhibitor sets loose the savage Hulk. The Hulk overpowers Spider-Man until Peter tells him who he is, and the Hulk, who somehow still knows him as a friend, lets go. Bruce is taken to a hospital for psychiatric care.
findings.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:_Brand_New_Day (Plot); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bruce_Banner_(Marvel_Cinematic_Universe) (Meeting Peter Parker and return of Savage Hulk); Looper / Nerdist / ComicBasics articles on Hulk in Brand New Day
findings.recheck: Jean possesses Banner and his inhibitor is removed; "when she lets go" and "broken" had no source.

findings.current: Mob boss Silvermane wants the Spider on his side as he schemes to rig the city's election, while Dr. Faber, a scientist unlocking hidden mutations in First World War veterans to save her son, kidnaps Ben for his DNA. Silvermane's men become monsters: Flint Marko turns into the Sandman and Dirk into Megawatt.
findings.problem: Several details are off. The veterans were mutated by German experiments on prisoners of war; Dr. Faber is trying to cure them (her son Ogden is one), and it is Ogden who drugs Ben and brings him to her lab. Marko can already turn to sand when he is introduced as Cat's bodyguard (a former Silvermane enforcer who rejoins him), and Dirk Leyden is a criminal Marko frees. Silvermane's fight is with Mayor Morris's re-election campaign; he warns Ben to keep the Spider out of it rather than recruiting him.
findings.suggested: 1933 New York. Ben Reilly, a worn-out private eye, was once the masked vigilante called the Spider. A case for nightclub singer Cat Hardy pulls him into mob boss Silvermane's war on Mayor Morris's re-election, fought with First World War veterans mutated by German experiments: Flint Marko, who turns to sand, Lonnie Lincoln, with armored skin, and Dirk Leyden, who stores electricity. Dr. Faber, hunting a cure for her son, has Ben drugged and studies him, and an antidote comes of it. Cat, who betrayed Ben's secret hoping to cure Marko, kills Silvermane, and the Spider kills Leyden. Ben gives his last antidote to Marko so he and Cat can be together, and opens Reilly and Ruiz Investigations with his secretary Janet.

findings.problem: X-Men '97 season 2 aired July 1 to August 12, 2026, but the app has a single X-Men '97 title. Season gating (ATL_SEAS) only works for titles named "<Show> S1/S2", so the "In season 2," prefix gates nothing: anyone who checks X-Men '97 after season 1 sees season 2 events (Magneto's death, Gambit as Death, X-Corp, Creed elected). findings.suggested: Split the title into "X-Men '97 S1" and "X-Men '97 S2" (as with Loki S1/S2) in alltitles and the chapter lists, and keep the "In season N," prefixes. If it stays one title, update its summary to cover season 2.
findings.dtext: Revised by your rule (seasons are split only where other titles come between them). Story order and the FoX-Men box keep one "X-Men '97" title, because the seasons run back to back. Release order splits it into "X-Men '97 S1" (2024, where it is now) and "X-Men '97 S2" (2026, between Spider-Noir and Spider-Man: Brand New Day), as What If...? already does. Needed: the two season titles in alltitles and the episode counts (10 and 9); a SPLIT entry mapping an old release-order tick to S1 only, so nobody is shown season 2 early; and "In season 1," or "In season 2," on the 48 Raft and 68 Compound X-Men '97 steps that have no prefix (the Collection's already do).
